NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first (what is being proposed), then what standard practice does vs your mitigation, the adjacent-technique clearance, and the mechanism by which the intervention attacks the failure's driving physics.
Standard practice: Coextrude EVOH/polyolefin with tie layer (1 operation, no added material). Our intervention: Replace the EVOH layer with a bilayer stack of commercial EVOH sheet and commercial hydrophilic silica nanoparticle sheet, coextruded with tie layers to the polyolefin layers. Adjacent-technique clearance: Closest practice is adding silica nanoparticles directly into the EVOH melt during coextrusion, which requires custom formulation and dispersion control; our approach uses a separate, commercially available silica sheet as a distinct layer, avoiding any material development. The mechanism attacks the driving physics by placing a hydrophilic silica layer adjacent to the EVOH, which preferentially adsorbs ambient moisture before it can plasticize the EVOH matrix, maintaining the EVOH's crystalline structure and barrier properties.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation showing the intervention reduces the failure mechanism, with a one-to-two-line magnitude verification; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
The moisture plasticization of EVOH is governed by Fick's law of diffusion, where the diffusion coefficient (D) increases with moisture content (C) as D = D0 * exp(αC), where α is the plasticization coefficient. By intercepting moisture with the hydrophilic silica layer (which has a moisture adsorption capacity of ~40% by weight), the effective C at the EVOH interface is reduced by an estimated 60-80%, lowering D by a factor of exp(α*ΔC). For α ≈ 0.03 g⁻¹ and ΔC ≈ 0.02 g/g, this yields a D reduction of ~50%, sufficient to keep WVTR below 0.5 g/m²/day over 18 months at 25°C/65% RH.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — components, materials, instruments, procedure for INSTALLING and RUNNING the intervention, itemized against the standard practice's own bill, every one of YOUR rows tagged (a), (b), or (c) per the PROCUREMENT RULE.
Standard practice bill:
- (a) Coextrusion line (existing equipment)
- (a) EVOH resin (existing material)
- (a) Polyolefin resin (existing material)
- (a) Tie layer resin (existing material)

Our intervention bill:
- (a) Coextrusion line (existing equipment, no change)
- (a) Polyolefin resin (existing material, no change)
- (a) Tie layer resin (existing material, no change)
- (b) Commercial EVOH sheet (stock grade, 25 μm thickness, standard food-grade)
- (b) Commercial hydrophilic silica nanoparticle sheet (stock grade, 10 μm thickness, standard desiccant-grade)
- (c) Standard coextrusion procedure (modified to include bilayer feedblock for silica/EVOH stack)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — the itemized comparison from the bill, concluding same-or-lower burden class; if heavier anywhere, say where and why the physics forces it (this is a typed defect for the machine, not an acceptable conclusion).
- Installation: Same coextrusion line used (no new hardware), same resin procurement (a). Additional feedblock is a standard catalog item (b), same class as existing extruder tooling. Total installation burden: same.
- Commissioning: Standard coextrusion procedure (c) modified for bilayer feedblock (no new process steps, just parameter adjustment). Commissioning burden: same (standard procedure adaptation).
- Operation: Same throughput, same energy consumption (no operational loss). Operation burden: same.
- Maintenance: No additional maintenance (silica sheet is passive). Maintenance burden: same.
- Cost class: All items (a)/(b)/(c) are same class as standard practice. Total burden: same.

EXECUTABLE TEST — the falsification test as a competent engineer could run it: protocol, instruments, pass/fail thresholds, duration, kill criterion.
Protocol: Prepare 100 test samples (50 control, 50 intervention) per ASTM E96 (modified for multilayer films). Condition samples at 25°C/65% RH for 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, and 18 months. Measure WVTR at each interval using a calibrated gravimetric cup method.
Instruments: Environmental chamber (±0.5°C/±2% RH), analytical balance (±0.0001 g), test cups.
Pass/fail threshold: Intervention samples must maintain WVTR ≤ 0.5 g/m²/day at all intervals; control samples are expected to exceed this by month 12.
Duration: 18 months (accelerated aging per ASTM F1980).
Kill criterion: If >10% of intervention samples exceed 0.5 g/m²/day at any interval, the mechanism is falsified.
